record.paper_title: Open problems on billiards and geometric optics
record.original_question: Let δ be a number in (0, π/2). A smooth closed strictly convex curve is said to have the δ-Gutkin property when, for the Birkhoff billiard inside the curve, the family of incoming oriented lines making the constant angle δ forms an invariant curve of the billiard map. What are the analogues of such Gutkin billiards on the sphere and on the hyperbolic plane?

evidence.quote: E. Gutkin studied those billiards in the plane [17]. Here we ask what the Gutkin billiards are on the sphere and the hyperbolic plane.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix δ ∈ (0, π/2). For a smooth, closed, strictly convex curve γ in a complete simply connected surface M of constant curvature, consider the Birkhoff billiard map T inside γ: an oriented chord (a directed geodesic segment with both endpoints on γ) is mapped to its reflection at the second endpoint, where the angle of incidence with the tangent line to γ equals the angle of reflection. Identify the space of oriented chords with the open annulus parametrized by (arclength on γ, angle with the tangent), so that T is a twist map of this annulus. Call γ a δ-Gutkin curve if the set of oriented chords that meet γ at the constant angle δ is an invariant curve of T (equivalently, if a chord enters γ at angle δ then it exits γ at angle δ).

In the Euclidean plane (M = R^2), a complete description of δ-Gutkin curves is known (Gutkin's class of curves with the constant-angle invariant property).

Problem: Describe and classify the δ-Gutkin curves when M is the round 2-sphere S^2 and when M is the hyperbolic plane H^2. In particular, characterize, up to isometry, all smooth closed strictly convex curves on S^2 and on H^2 possessing the δ-Gutkin property for some δ ∈ (0, π/2), and determine for which values of δ such curves exist.
artifact.category_tag: Birkhoff billiards on surfaces of constant curvature
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of describing Gutkin billiards on the sphere and the hyperbolic plane appears to remain open. Available work has addressed related questions (hyperbolicity of billiards on surfaces of constant curvature, and rigidity of higher-dimensional Gutkin tables), and only first steps via infinitesimal deformations of the circle with the Gutkin property are reported, but no full classification on S^2 or H^2 has been established.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems on Billiards and Geometric Optics
status_evidence.snippet: Gutkin studied those billiards in the plane. Here we ask what the Gutkin billiards are on the sphere and the hyperbolic plane.
status_evidence.claim: The question is posed as an open problem in the survey on billiards and geometric optics.

status_evidence.title: Gutkin billiard tables in higher dimensions and rigidity
status_evidence.snippet: Rigidity-type results for Gutkin billiard tables in higher dimensions.
status_evidence.claim: Related rigidity work concerns higher-dimensional analogues, not the 2D constant-curvature classification.

status_evidence.title: Hyperbolic Billiards on Surfaces of Constant Curvature
status_evidence.snippet: Conditions for hyperbolicity of billiards on the sphere and hyperbolic plane.
status_evidence.claim: Existing work on billiards on S^2 and H^2 addresses hyperbolicity, not the Gutkin constant-angle invariant curve property.
